D_server_side_logic.additional_logic:
1. Tool types and annotations: Catalogue-listed actions include reads and writes. Annotation fields (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) were not published. The catalogue labels moveContent destructive and says confirmation is recommended; this is not evidence of server enforcement.
2. Confirmation: Catalogue instructions recommend user confirmation for moves and instruct agents to ask before selecting project region or subscription. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or approval protocol was evidenced.
3. Permissions: Datasite says the server respects existing product permissions and scopes AI responses to data-room content the user can access. OAuth details and token properties are unavailable. The companion skill says Blueflame content search requires project activation and eligible-user access.
4. Modes and boundaries: No documented MCP read-only mode, toolset filter, allowlist, or public regional MCP endpoints. Catalogue instructions specify PREPARE staging-folder restrictions and state publishing is unsupported there. Project setup instructions require an explicit datacenter choice.
5. Data protection: Datasite says documents stay in its environment and AI responses are scoped to accessible data-room content. API Program Terms also warn that applications may transmit data outside Datasite and may access, modify, or delete it.
6. Limits: Catalogue descriptions specify search results capped at 25; folder listing depth 1–5 and per-folder limit 1,000; synchronous moves up to 100 items, with larger moves asynchronous if bulk move is enabled. Terms prohibit excessive or abusive use but give no numeric rate limit.
7. Validation/correction: Catalogue instructions give parameter constraints and routing guidance. No server code is available to determine rejection, coercion, or operator overrides.
8. Logging/telemetry: Datasite claims complete audit trails for actions and AI interactions. Public evidence does not document telemetry payloads, opt-out, or retention.
9. Vendor-interest mechanisms: The discovered 26 tool names contain no feedback, rating, survey, or report tools. Datasite offers sales/demo links on its website; no evidence ties those prompts to MCP tool results.
10. Behaviour shaping: The external skill pack supplies instructions and tool-selection rules. Catalogue tool descriptions also instruct agents, including when to ask, which tools to call first, and what to tell users. Server enforcement is unknown.
11. Memory/state: No evidence that prior agent behavior changes later outputs or available tools.
12. Structure: Public evidence describes one hosted endpoint and a flat catalogue tool surface; no sub-server hierarchy documented.
13. Escape hatches: No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or generic request tool found in the catalogued names.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official public machine tool list was found in Datasite’s official pages, repository, or prepared evidence. The Claude connector directory lists 19 names; Manufact reports 19; Agent Discoverability reports 25. Their union yields 26 distinct names: 18 shared between Claude and Agent Discoverability, seven additional Agent Discoverability names, and acceptDisclaimer found in Claude but absent from the 25-name list. All names are third-party-confirmed; actions.json records the source for each. MCP.so displays no tool list. No official total is published.

Public evidence does not provide a complete product/API operation inventory for further comparison.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The external skills instruct agents to ask for missing transaction context, read project details first, and use searchDocuments as the only document-content source. Datasite’s public pages encourage natural-language use but do not publish equivalent server-side enforcement evidence. Catalogue guidance includes user confirmation before moves and explicit region selection.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Datasite states: “Documents never leave Datasite's secure environment,” “Every action is captured in a complete audit trail,” and “AI responses are scoped to your data room content only.” Its API Program Terms separately warn that application use may transmit data outside Datasite and that application providers may access, disclose, modify, or delete Datasite data.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Datasite describes the connector as operating within existing access controls, allowing teams to use AI assistants without exporting sensitive documents. It says users can connect preferred assistants including Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and Blueflame AI.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: No public server implementation or OAuth metadata was available to verify the advertised controls. Tool descriptions in a third-party catalogue specify boundaries such as PREPARE staging-folder use, access-dependent search, and asynchronous bulk moves; these are catalogue evidence, not independently verified server enforcement. Datasite’s own API Program Terms qualify data-protection claims for third-party applications.

contradictions: Datasite’s official marketing page says deal documents never leave the Datasite environment; the API Program Terms warn that application use may transmit data outside Datasite and that application providers may access, disclose, modify, or delete data.

Third-party catalogues disagree on tool count: Claude and Manufact report 19 tools, while Agent Discoverability reports 25. Their discovered union contains 26 distinct names; no official tool list or official total was found.
OAuth is reported by third-party connector listings, while the pre-fetched OAuth evidence says metadata was not fetched because the input endpoint is unpublished and per-customer.
observations_for_research: The public tool inventory varies across catalogues and includes detailed agent-facing workflow rules, but no accessible official tool schemas or hosted implementation were found.
The companion skills distribute substantial behavior guidance outside the MCP server; one skill repository describes tiered dependence on Datasite Blueflame AI features.
notes: Reviewed the prepared links.json, links_check.txt, pages/, code/, OAuth note, official Datasite MCP page, official news/event pages, pricing page, API Program Terms, privacy notice, official-linked skills repository, and catalogues.
